title: Define and prove geometry, borders, depth, and controls
objective: Turn the approved control direction and canonical typography, colour, and spatial foundations into a coherent Mez geometry, border, depth, and interaction system with accessible production-ready control states.

included: semantic radius and shape roles for controls, cards, panels, fields, tags, and contained objects
hairline, border, divider, shadow, elevation, focus, and contained-dark contracts
button, link, icon-only, input, select, textarea, checkbox, radio, switch, and destructive-control states
default, hover, focus, active, loading, disabled, error, destructive, and mobile control behaviour
adversarial fixtures for long labels, icons, localisation, keyboard navigation, forced colours, reduced motion, and touch targets
generated tokens, schema, guidance, and a bounded primary-control and surface-grammar proof
excluded: changing canonical typography, colour, spacing, widths, breakpoints, density, or responsive rules
product-expression objects and Living Core treatment
consumer migration and production Figma library

acceptance: one semantic source generates geometry, border, depth, focus, and control-state contracts
canonical FND-01, FND-02, and FND-03 values remain unchanged
bounded package authority and approval state are mechanically verifiable
primary, secondary, text, icon-only, form, destructive, loading, disabled, dark-surface, mobile, and accessibility fixtures are realistic
micro-lift and restrained alternative finishes are compared without gradients becoming generic decoration
human verdict can be recorded without changing unrelated foundations

verification.passCondition: source, generated tokens, control contracts, and task records validate
every control exposes the required interaction, disabled, loading, destructive, error, focus, and contained-dark states
keyboard, focus, forced-colour, reduced-motion, touch-target, long-label, localisation, and 320px fixtures remain usable
Olli approves the primary-button finish and complete surface grammar

humanGate.approvalQuestion: Does this geometry, border, depth, and control system feel premium, restrained, recognisably Mez, and production-useful across interaction states and surfaces?

stopConditions: a geometry or control rule requires changing canonical typography, colour, or spatial values
focus, disabled, loading, destructive, error, mobile, keyboard, or forced-colour behaviour is missing
a gradient or glow becomes generic control decoration instead of protected product identity
the proof combines product-expression or homepage decisions with the control-finish gate
notes: Begin with a read-only audit of the approved control calibration and current geometry, border, shadow, focus, and state conflicts.

The approved direction is 12px control radius, 48px default height, solid/outline/text hierarchy, restrained micro-lift, contained-dark behaviour, and mobile hierarchy; implementation and adversarial validation remain open.
FND-01 typography, FND-02 colour, and FND-03 space-layout are canonical inputs, not design variables for this task.
